promptTitle.apps: Scan to find apps and their leftovers
promptTitle.storage: Scan to see what’s using your storage
promptTitle.smartClean: Scan to find what can be cleaned

scanGate.promptSubtitle: A quick, local scan maps what’s on your Mac. Nothing is removed without your review.

selectionBar.willMove: {{size}} will be moved to the Trash

xcodeDerivedData.name: Xcode DerivedData
xcodeDerivedData.why: Intermediate build products Xcode regenerates automatically on the next build.
xcodeDerivedData.what: Your next build will take longer while Xcode re-indexes and recompiles.

xcodeArchives.name: Xcode Archives
xcodeArchives.why: Archived builds created for App Store submissions and TestFlight distribution.
xcodeArchives.what: You will lose the ability to re-export dSYMs or re-submit this exact build.

xcodeDeviceSupportIos.name: iOS Device Support
xcodeDeviceSupportIos.why: Debug symbols cached for physical iOS devices you connected in the past.
xcodeDeviceSupportIos.what: Xcode re-downloads device support the next time you connect that device.

xcodeDeviceSupportWatchos.name: watchOS Device Support
xcodeDeviceSupportWatchos.why: Debug symbols cached for paired Apple Watches you tested with in the past.
xcodeDeviceSupportWatchos.what: Xcode re-downloads device support the next time you connect that device.

xcodeSimulatorCaches.name: Simulator Caches
xcodeSimulatorCaches.why: Cached data the iOS/watchOS Simulator rebuilds automatically as needed.
xcodeSimulatorCaches.what: No impact — the simulator recreates its cache automatically.

xcodeSimulatorDevices.name: Simulator Devices
xcodeSimulatorDevices.why: Storage used by every simulated iOS/watchOS/tvOS device, including any test app data installed on them.
xcodeSimulatorDevices.what: Simulator devices and any app data installed on them will need to be recreated.

npmCache.name: npm cache
npmCache.why: Downloaded package tarballs npm keeps so future installs can skip the network.
npmCache.what: Future npm installs re-download packages instead of using the local cache.

yarnCache.name: Yarn cache
yarnCache.why: Downloaded package cache Yarn keeps across all your projects.
yarnCache.what: Installs fall back to the network; already-installed projects are unaffected.

pnpmStore.name: pnpm store
pnpmStore.why: Shared package store pnpm keeps across all your projects.
pnpmStore.what: Installs fall back to the network; already-installed projects are unaffected.

metroCache.name: Metro bundler cache
metroCache.why: Temporary bundler cache Metro (React Native) writes to your system temp folder.
metroCache.what: Clear it from your project with "npx react-native start --reset-cache" — it lives in a system folder MacBook Cleaner never touches.

gradleCaches.name: Gradle caches
gradleCaches.why: Downloaded dependencies and build metadata shared across Android/Gradle projects.
gradleCaches.what: Gradle re-downloads and re-resolves dependencies on the next build (slower first build).

androidAvd.name: Android emulator images
androidAvd.why: Virtual device images and any data installed on your Android emulators.
androidAvd.what: You will need to re-create any emulator you use again, and any test app data on them is lost.

cocoapodsCache.name: CocoaPods cache
cocoapodsCache.why: Downloaded pod specs and sources cached across all your iOS projects.
cocoapodsCache.what: "pod install" re-downloads pods the next time it runs.

unknown.why: Storage used by a developer tool detected on this Mac.
unknown.what: Review before removing — the tool may need to regenerate this data.

browser.name: {{browser}} cache & temporary files
browser.why: Cached site assets and rendering data the browser rebuilds automatically.
browser.what: Sites reload full assets on your next visit — passwords, cookies, and bookmarks are untouched.
browser.notCleanedYet: Not cleaned via this app yet

duplicate.why: This file appears to match another file we found, by size and a content sample from its start and end.
duplicate.what: Only this copy would be affected — nothing else is touched, and this is a candidate match, not a guaranteed exact duplicate.

installer.why: An installer downloaded from the internet.
installer.what: Re-download the installer if you need to reinstall this software.

archive.what: If you already extracted its contents elsewhere, the archive itself is usually safe to remove.

large.why: A large file we found in your files — we could not determine a more specific type.

download.why: A file sitting in your Downloads folder.

file.yourFile: This is your file — review it before removing anything.

system.logsWhy: Log files an app or macOS wrote automatically.
system.cacheWhy: Cache data an app or macOS created automatically to speed up repeat launches.
system.what: No impact — regenerated automatically as needed.

sensitive.devWhat: This item’s name suggests it may contain sensitive data. Protected by default — review manually in Finder.
sensitive.systemWhat: This item’s name suggests it may be sensitive — protected by default.
sensitive.fileWhy: This item's name suggests it may contain sensitive or important data.
sensitive.fileWhat: Protected by default — review manually in Finder before ever considering removal.

meet.title: Meet MacBook Cleaner
meet.body: Keep your Mac clean, fast and clutter-free.

space.title: See What’s Taking Space
space.body: Find large files, old downloads, junk and forgotten app data.

safe.title: Clean Safely
safe.body: Review everything before anything gets removed.

permission.title: One optional permission
permission.body: macOS keeps some locations — like app caches, the Trash and Mail data — private unless you grant Full Disk Access. MacBook Cleaner works without it, but sees less.
permission.local: Scanning happens entirely on this Mac. Nothing is uploaded.
permission.folders: macOS may also ask before MacBook Cleaner reads Downloads, Documents and Desktop. Allowing it lets us find large and duplicate files there.
permission.changeLater: You can change this anytime in System Settings → Privacy & Security.

photos.label: Photos
photos.description: Your Pictures folder, including the Photos library

cache.label: Cache
cache.description: App caches and logs in your Library

other.label: Other
other.description: Music, mail, messages and other app data

systemData.label: System Data
systemData.description: macOS, snapshots and space we can’t attribute to a folder

systemJunk.title: System Junk
systemJunk.description: App and system caches that rebuild themselves automatically.

browser.title: Browser Caches
browser.description: Cached web pages and images. Passwords, cookies and bookmarks are untouched.

appLeftovers.title: App Leftovers
appLeftovers.description: Caches left behind by apps that are no longer installed.

logs.title: Logs & Crash Reports
logs.description: Diagnostic logs apps write over time. Safe to clear.

developer.title: Developer Junk
developer.description: Build products and package caches your tools can re-create.

oldDownloads.title: Old Downloads
oldDownloads.description: Installers, archives and files you downloaded a while ago. Your call — nothing is preselected.

smartClean.intro: One scan finds caches, leftovers, logs and forgotten downloads. You review everything before anything is removed.
smartClean.safeRightAway: {{size}} is safe to clean right away. The rest is yours to review.
smartClean.tidyTitle: Your Mac is already looking tidy
smartClean.tidySubtitle: We didn’t find anything worth cleaning right now. Check back in a week or turn on Scheduled Cleanup.
smartClean.trashNote: Already in your Trash. Empty it in Finder when you’re sure — MacBook Cleaner never empties it for you.
smartClean.restoreNote: Moved to Trash — you can restore anything.

dashboard.subtitle: Your Mac deserves a little cleanup.
dashboard.moreWaiting: {{size}} more is waiting for your review.
dashboard.findSafeBody: Caches, leftovers, old downloads and more — reviewed by you.
dashboard.noCleanups: No cleanups yet — your first one is a click away.
dashboard.trashEmpty: Empty it in Finder to reclaim this space
dashboard.trashNeedsAccess: Needs Full Disk Access to measure

storage.subtitle: Understand what’s actually using your Mac’s storage.
storage.noItems: No individual items large enough to list here.
storage.showingLargest: Showing the largest items we found (files {{size}} and up).

explain.photos: Your Photos library is managed by the Photos app, so MacBook Cleaner never removes individual photos from it. To save space, turn on Photos → Settings → iCloud → Optimize Mac Storage.
explain.other: Music, Mail, Messages attachments and data apps keep in your Library. Most of it is managed by those apps — clean it from inside them.
explain.systemData: macOS itself, Time Machine local snapshots, virtual memory and anything we couldn’t attribute to a folder. macOS manages this space and frees snapshots automatically when it needs room.

largeFiles.subtitle: Find forgotten files consuming gigabytes of space.
largeFiles.emptySubtitle: Your Mac is already looking tidy.
largeFiles.footnote: Searched Downloads, Desktop, Documents and Movies. App libraries (Photos, iMovie, Final Cut) are never opened.

downloads.subtitle: Tidy up installers, archives and files you downloaded and forgot.
downloads.emptySubtitle: Nothing over {{size}} is waiting in Downloads. Nice.

duplicates.subtitle: Identical files, confirmed byte-for-byte. One copy is always kept.
duplicates.oneKept: At least one copy is always kept.
duplicates.matchedBy: Matched by size, then by a full-content checksum.

native.protectedSystem: This is a protected macOS location ({{path}}) and can’t be removed.
native.homeFolder: Your home folder itself can never be removed.
native.protectedFolder: {{path}} is a protected folder and can’t be removed as a whole.
native.outsideHome: Only files inside your home folder can be removed.
native.sensitive: This item may contain sensitive data, so it’s protected.
native.noAccess: Couldn’t access this item — permission was denied or it’s already gone.
native.rootFolder: A root folder can’t be removed.
native.trashFailed: Couldn’t move this item to the Trash.
native.notApp: This isn’t an app that can be uninstalled.
native.notInApplications: Only apps directly inside an Applications folder can be uninstalled.
native.systemApp: Apple apps are part of macOS and are protected.
native.previewHomeOnly: Preview is only available for files in your home folder.
native.loginDevBuild: Launch at Login is only available in the installed app, not in a development build.
native.notInstalled: MacBook Cleaner is running from a disk image or your Downloads folder. Move it to Applications, open it from there, then try again.
native.scheduleFailed: macOS couldn’t start the scheduled cleanup helper.
native.appMoved: This app is no longer at that location.
native.noAppSupport: MacBook Cleaner couldn’t access its own data folder.
native.protectedProcess: This is a protected system process and can't be quit.
native.notOwnProcess: Only your own processes can be quit.
native.quitRefused: macOS refused to quit this application.
native.licenseNotActive: This license key isn’t active yet. If you just purchased it, check your email in a moment and try again.
native.licenseNotFound: This license key wasn’t found. Double-check it and try again.
native.licenseLimitReached: This license key is already activated on another Mac. Deactivate it there first, then try again here.
native.licenseNetworkError: Couldn’t reach the licensing server. Check your internet connection and try again.
native.licenseServerError: The licensing server returned something unexpected. Try again in a moment.

apps.subtitle: Remove applications together with their caches, logs and leftovers.
apps.emptySubtitle: We couldn’t read your Applications folder.
apps.noLeftovers: No caches, logs or supporting files found for this app.
apps.explainer: Caches and logs are safe to clear. Supporting files and preferences hold your settings and data for this app — clearing them resets it. Quit the app before cleaning or uninstalling.

systemJunk.subtitle: Caches, logs and temporary files your Mac rebuilds on its own.
systemJunk.safeBody: Rebuilt automatically when needed. No personal data.
systemJunk.reviewBody: Removable, but may mean re-downloads, rebuilds or sign-outs.
systemJunk.emptySubtitle: Your caches and logs are already lean.
systemJunk.safeSubtitle: App caches, browser caches and logs
systemJunk.developerSubtitle: Xcode, simulators, package managers and build caches
systemJunk.devHidden: {{size}} of developer caches hidden. <link>Turn on Developer Cleanup</link>

settings.subtitle: Make MacBook Cleaner work the way you like.
settings.themeSubtitle: Follow macOS or pick a look.
settings.languageChosen: Stays the same whatever your Mac’s language is.
settings.launchAtLoginSubtitle: Open MacBook Cleaner when you log in.
settings.moveToTrashSubtitle: Always on. MacBook Cleaner never permanently deletes anything — you stay in control of emptying the Trash.
settings.confirmBeforeSubtitle: When off, cleanups made only of Safe items skip the confirmation. Your own files and Review items always ask.
settings.developerSubtitle: Show Xcode, simulator, npm, Gradle and other build caches.
settings.exclusionsSubtitle: Files and folders here are never suggested for cleanup — manually or on a schedule.
settings.exclusionsInput: Folder or file path to exclude
settings.noExclusions: No exclusions yet. You can also hide any item from its row with the “never suggest” button.
settings.fdaGranted: Granted — MacBook Cleaner can measure everything it cleans.
settings.fdaOptional: Optional. Lets MacBook Cleaner see caches, the Trash and app data macOS keeps private.
settings.filesStay: Your files stay on your Mac
settings.filesStaySubtitle: Scanning happens locally. Nothing is uploaded, and file contents are only read to confirm duplicates.
settings.resetBody: This clears your settings, exclusions, schedule and cleanup history, and turns off scheduled cleanup. It never touches your files or the Trash.

performanceAlerts.title: Performance alerts
performanceAlerts.enabledSubtitle: Native notifications when an app's resource usage stays high. Turning this off disables every alert below.
performanceAlerts.highMemorySubtitle: Warn when a single app sustains more than this much memory.
performanceAlerts.highMemoryPercentSubtitle: Warn when a single app sustains more than this share of your Mac's total memory.
performanceAlerts.backgroundCpuSubtitle: Warn when a background app (no Dock icon) sustains more than this much CPU.
performanceAlerts.criticalPressureSubtitle: Warn when macOS reports memory pressure as critical.

license.title: License
license.deactivateConfirmBody: This frees up your license so you can activate it on another Mac. You can always reactivate it here again later.

scheduleScreen.subtitle: Keep unnecessary clutter under control automatically.
scheduleScreen.howOftenSubtitle: MacBook Cleaner checks quietly in the background — no window opens.
scheduleScreen.remindBody: Send a notification when there’s enough to clean or space is running low.
scheduleScreen.autoBody: Move eligible developer caches to the Trash, then tell you what was cleaned.
scheduleScreen.eligibleSubtitle: Only caches and junk can ever be scheduled.

categories.developerDetail: Xcode DerivedData, npm, Yarn, pnpm, Gradle, CocoaPods
categories.systemDetail: Caches and logs in your Library
categories.browserDetail: Safari, Chrome, Edge and Firefox caches

scheduleScreen.onlyTrash: Scheduled runs only ever move items to the Trash.
scheduleScreen.needsApplications: Scheduling needs MacBook Cleaner to live in your Applications folder.

consent.title: Turn on automatic cleaning?
consent.intro: While you’re away, MacBook Cleaner will move these to the Trash — and nothing else:
consent.limits: Runs only when there’s at least {{min}} to clean, never more than {{max}} or {{items}} items at once, always skips your exclusions, and sends you a summary. Everything stays in the Trash until you empty it.

toasts.excluded: Got it — that item won’t be suggested again.
toasts.quickLookPreview: Quick Look opens here in the desktop app.
toasts.scheduleSaved: Schedule saved — MacBook Cleaner will keep an eye on things.

language.title: Language
language.subtitle: Changes apply instantly — no restart needed.

cleanup.willMove_one: {{count}} item will be moved to the Trash, so you can put it back until you empty it.
cleanup.willMove_other: {{count}} items will be moved to the Trash, so you can put anything back until you empty it.
cleanup.notPermanent: Moved to Trash — nothing is permanently deleted.
cleanup.personalWarning_one: {{count}} of these is your own file — please make sure you don’t need it.
cleanup.personalWarning_other: {{count}} of these are your own files or app settings — please make sure you don’t need them.
cleanup.reviewWarning_one: {{count}} item may cause re-downloads, rebuilds or sign-outs.
cleanup.reviewWarning_other: {{count}} items may cause re-downloads, rebuilds or sign-outs.
cleanup.ack: I’ve reviewed these items and want to move them to the Trash.
cleanup.breathingRoom: Your Mac has more breathing room.
cleanup.recoverable: Everything went to the Trash, so it’s recoverable. The space is fully released once you empty the Trash.

performance.subtitle: See how your Mac is doing — CPU, memory, apps, battery and more.
performance.runningAppsSubtitle: Which apps are using the most memory and CPU right now.
performance.cpuUsageTip: The share of your Mac's total processing power in use, measured every couple of seconds across all cores.
performance.cpuChart: CPU usage over the last 60 seconds

cpuParts.userTip: Time spent running apps and your own processes.
cpuParts.systemTip: Time spent inside macOS itself — drivers, file system, networking.
cpuParts.idleTip: Processing power that is free right now.

performance.memoryUsedTip: App memory + wired + compressed — the same “Memory Used” figure Activity Monitor shows. Cached files aren’t counted because macOS frees them instantly when needed.
performance.memoryChart: Memory used over the last 60 seconds
performance.pressureTip: macOS's own gauge of whether apps have the memory they need. High usage with “Normal” pressure is healthy — macOS uses spare RAM on purpose.

memParts.appTip: Memory your apps are actively using.
memParts.wiredTip: Memory macOS itself needs and can’t move or compress.
memParts.compressedTip: Memory macOS has compressed to make room — a normal, efficient technique.
memParts.cachedTip: Recently used files macOS keeps in memory to open them faster. Freed automatically whenever an app needs the space.
memParts.swapTip: Memory macOS has temporarily moved to your SSD. Some swap is normal; a lot of it alongside high memory pressure means your Mac would benefit from fewer open apps.

health.title: Mac Health
health.subtitle: A plain-language summary. Every status comes straight from macOS.
health.memoryTip: Memory pressure is macOS's own measure of how hard it's working to free memory. “Normal” means apps have the memory they need, even if most RAM is in use.
health.storageTip: Below {{full}} free is shown as “Getting full” and below {{low}} as “Running low” — macOS needs free space for updates, caches and virtual memory.
health.batteryTip: The battery condition macOS reports — the same one shown in System Settings → Battery.
health.cpuTip: How much of your Mac's total processing power is in use right now, across all cores.
health.uptimeTip: How long your Mac has been running since it last started up. Restarting now and then lets macOS finish installing updates.
health.macosTip: Based on the result of macOS’s own automatic Software Update check. MacBook Cleaner doesn’t contact Apple’s servers itself.

os.kernelTip: The open-source core macOS is built on. Mostly useful for troubleshooting.
os.noUpdatesFound: macOS found no updates the last time it checked.
os.openToCheck: Open Software Update to check for the latest version of macOS.
os.lastChecked: macOS last checked {{when}}. MacBook Cleaner reads this result; it never contacts Apple itself.

battery.maxCapacityTip: How much charge the battery can hold now compared with when it was new. Reported by macOS — the same value as System Settings → Battery → Battery Health.
battery.capacityNote: Capacity naturally decreases as a battery ages. MacBook Cleaner only reports it — no app can restore battery capacity.
battery.cyclesOfDesign: {{cycles}} of {{design}} cycles the battery reports it was designed for
battery.cycleExplain: Battery cycle count represents the number of full charge cycles your Mac battery has completed. Using 100% of the battery’s capacity — even across several partial charges — counts as one cycle.
battery.timeTip: macOS only provides an estimate once it has observed your current usage for a while.
battery.conditionTip: Reported by macOS. “Normal” means the battery is working as expected; “Service Recommended” means Apple suggests having it checked.
battery.designCapacityTip: How much charge the battery held when it was new.
battery.fullCapacityTip: How much charge the battery holds today when full.

apps.cpuTip: Share of your Mac's total processing power. Activity Monitor shows per-core values instead, which can go above 100%.
apps.memoryTip: Physical memory footprint — the figure Activity Monitor's Memory column shows. Apps include their helper processes.
apps.footnote_one: {{count}} process on this Mac. Apps include their helper processes. macOS doesn’t let apps read CPU and memory for other users’ system processes, so those show “—”.
apps.footnote_other: {{count}} processes on this Mac. Apps include their helper processes. macOS doesn’t let apps read CPU and memory for other users’ system processes, so those show “—”.

details.title: {{name}} details
details.cpuTip: Share of your Mac's total processing power right now.
details.memoryTip: Physical memory footprint, including helper processes.
details.threadsTip: Independent tasks the app is running at the same time. Busy apps commonly use dozens.
details.quitHint: Quit asks the app to close normally — it may still prompt you to save unsaved work. Force Quit skips that and should only be used if the app is unresponsive.
details.quitUnavailableSystem: System processes can't be quit from here.
details.forceQuitConfirmBody: Any unsaved work in this app will be lost, and this can't be undone.
details.quitStillRunning: {{name}} may still be closing — it could be waiting on an unsaved-changes dialog.

mac.modelIdTip: Apple's internal name for this exact Mac model — handy when looking up specs or support articles.
mac.hostnameTip: Your Mac's name on the local network. Shown here only — never sent anywhere.
mac.rosetta: MacBook Cleaner is running under Rosetta
mac.localNote: All of this is read locally from macOS and stays on your Mac. MacBook Cleaner doesn’t read your serial number.

notifications.highMemoryBody: {{app}} is currently using {{size}} of RAM. Open MacBook Cleaner to review application resource usage.
notifications.backgroundCpuBody: {{app}} is using {{percent}}% CPU in the background. Open MacBook Cleaner to review application resource usage.
notifications.pressureBody: Your Mac's memory is under heavy pressure. Closing a few apps can help. Open MacBook Cleaner to review application resource usage.

background.title: Background Resource Usage
background.subtitle: The background apps using the most CPU and memory right now.
background.none: No background apps are using notable resources.

recommendations.title: Recommendations
recommendations.subtitle: Based on what's measured right now — not guarantees.
recommendations.criticalPressure: Your Mac's memory pressure is critical. Closing a few apps can help free it up.
recommendations.warningPressure: Memory pressure is elevated. Keeping fewer apps open can help.
recommendations.backgroundCpu: {{count}} background apps are using significant CPU.
recommendations.swap: Swap usage is elevated ({{percent}} of available swap).

titles.licensedInvalid: Your license is no longer valid

bodies.trialExpired: Your 48-hour free trial is over. Buy a lifetime license to keep using MacBook Cleaner, or activate a license key if you already have one.
bodies.licensedInvalid: Dodo Payments reported that this license key is no longer active — it may have been refunded or deactivated. Activate a different key, or buy a new lifetime license.
bodies.licensedGraceExpired: MacBook Cleaner couldn’t confirm your license is still valid. Connect to the internet and refresh, or activate your key again.

paywall.tamperNotice: Your trial data couldn’t be verified, so it’s being treated as expired.
paywall.activateLabel: Already purchased? Enter your license key

toasts.activateSuccess: License activated — thank you for your support!
toasts.deactivateSuccess: License deactivated. You can activate it on another Mac now.

notifications.autoCleanDone: Auto-clean moved {{size}} of safe cache data to the Trash.
notifications.autoCleanPartial: Auto-clean moved {{size}} to the Trash. Some items couldn’t be moved ({{failed}}).
notifications.lowSpace: Your Mac has only {{size}} free. Review storage recommendations.

native.appleEventsUsage: MacBook Cleaner asks Finder to move the items you approve to the Trash, so you can restore them until you empty it.
